report.summary: The reboot crash is a Wi-Fi driver fault triggered from our event-loop dispatch: STA_START is now answered on the product's own task and commissioning restarts the radio in STA mode instead of configuring a station on a live APSTA interface. Builds at 2.94 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: The mdns idle crash did not reproduce (2.5 min idle clean). The review is still right that CONFIG_MDNS_TASK_STACK_SIZE never reaches the generated header — the mdns Kconfig is not part of this build — so I have not replaced that with a claim; mDNS is already non-fatal (the settings page is served from httpd regardless) and the remaining exposure is the hostname only.

The new failure is a different animal from the last three: a CPU cache fault at an unmapped PC inside the Wi-Fi driver's station start, not a stack overflow. Re-reading it as 'our code called into the Wi-Fi management path from the framework's dispatch' points at the one place we do that: STA_START answered with esp_wifi_connect() on the loop task. The connect now happens on the net task, like every other Wi-Fi action of ours.

Also removed the APSTA commissioning path: the onboarding AP now brings the radio up in AP mode alone, and commissioning stops the radio and starts it again in station mode from the task that asked — the documented way to change an AP/STA mode with the driver in a known state, instead of configuring a station on a live APSTA interface.
Did not add another stack bump: the crashes since the queue fix have all been in the driver's own code path, which has no Kconfig stack of ours.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2cd330 (2937648 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; check_code clean

findingsAddressed.finding: fail — commissioned panel's reboot aborts with a CPU 'Cache error' inside ieee80211 station start
findingsAddressed.fix: the station is started from the mqtt_net task on STA_START instead of esp_wifi_connect() in the event handler; commissioning restarts the radio in STA mode from app_mqtt_set_wifi's caller task rather than configuring a station on a live APSTA interface

findingsAddressed.finding: warning — CONFIG_MDNS_TASK_STACK_SIZE absent from the generated header
findingsAddressed.fix: confirmed: the mdns Kconfig is not part of this build's Kconfigs, so the value cannot reach the image; mDNS stays non-fatal (httpd serves the settings page regardless) and the reported idle crash did not reproduce in this run

findingsAddressed.finding: info — standing deviations (single-button factory reset, plain-MQTT default broker, empty-payload TRV poll, three-number vocabulary)
findingsAddressed.fix: unchanged by design/owner choice; the voice vocabulary gap is flagged again for the owner

openQuestions: Whether the cache fault is a product sequencing problem or the emulated Wi-Fi driver faulting regardless cannot be decided from here; the next commissioned-reboot run is the test, and it either reaches the console twice in a row or the fault is in the emulator's driver.
mDNS on the real board still needs its own check, since its task stack cannot be configured through this build's Kconfig set.
